patient.chief_complaint: Stepwise cognitive decline over two years in a patient who cannot have an MRI
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Ottavio Pirelli is a 79-year-old retired customs officer who attends with his wife. She dates his decline to two events: two years ago he had an hour of right arm weakness, and eight months ago a day of right hand clumsiness with word-finding difficulty. Neither was imaged. After each he was permanently worse, and between them he was stable. He now cannot manage the household accounts he kept for decades, has twice missed medication doses, and stopped driving eight months ago. His memory improves when he is reminded of context; his difficulty is with organising and with finding words. He has a dual-chamber pacemaker implanted eleven years ago for complete atrioventricular block; the device is not MR-conditional and the manufacturer's documentation cannot be located, and he also has severe claustrophobia. There are no hallucinations, no fluctuation in alertness and no dream enactment. His blood pressure runs at 150-160 systolic.

findings: Dual-chamber pacing with atrial sensing and ventricular pacing at 68 bpm
Underlying atrial rhythm is sinus on the atrial channel
Repolarisation not interpretable during ventricular pacing
No atrial fibrillation on the atrial channel during the recording
ecg.interpretation: Normally functioning dual-chamber pacemaker with sinus rhythm on the atrial channel. Surface ECG interpretation is limited during pacing, but the device itself holds long-term atrial rhythm data, and interrogating it is the most informative available test for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.

labs.interpretation: LDL 96 mg/dL is above the secondary-prevention target. TSH, B12, folate, RPR and HIV are normal or negative, excluding reversible causes of the cognitive decline.

findings.location: Left frontal operculum and anterior insula
findings.description: Wedge-shaped cortical and subcortical low attenuation with ex vacuo widening of the adjacent sulci — chronic middle cerebral artery territory infarct
Cortical low attenuation with local volume loss — chronic infarct
Small rounded low-attenuation lesion consistent with an old lacune
Symmetric periventricular low attenuation consistent with chronic small-vessel disease; a Fazekas grade cannot be assigned reliably on CT
Ventricular and sulcal enlargement proportionate to age; medial temporal structures cannot be graded on CT

additional_observations: MRI was contraindicated: the pacemaker and leads are not MR-conditional and the manufacturer's documentation is unavailable, and the patient also has severe claustrophobia
CT identifies two chronic left hemispheric cortical infarcts and one right subcortical lacune, which with the stepwise history satisfies the vascular attribution
CT cannot show cerebral microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis, so cerebral amyloid angiopathy cannot be excluded — this matters because it would alter the antithrombotic decision
CT cannot grade medial temporal atrophy reliably, so a coexisting Alzheimer process cannot be excluded or supported on this study
ct.impression: Two chronic left middle cerebral artery territory cortical infarcts, one right subcortical lacune and moderate periventricular low attenuation. Sufficient to attribute the dementia to cerebrovascular disease. Explicit limitations: microbleeds and cortical superficial siderosis are invisible on CT, so amyloid angiopathy is not excluded, and medial temporal atrophy cannot be graded, so a coexisting degenerative process is neither supported nor excluded.

Interrogating the device already in the patient provided continuous rhythm data that no external monitor could match, and it establishes an anticoagulable second mechanism.

results.title: Diagnostic criteria for vascular cognitive disorders: a VASCOG statement
results.authors: Sachdev P, Kalaria R, O'Brien J, et al.
results.summary: Requires a cognitive syndrome documented on a validated instrument plus imaging or temporal evidence that cerebrovascular disease accounts for it.

results.authors: Duering M, Biessels GJ, Brodtmann A, et al.
results.summary: Defines and standardises the reporting of white matter hyperintensity, lacunes, microbleeds, perivascular spaces and cortical superficial siderosis.

vascular_cognitive_impairment.summary: No disease-modifying therapy exists for vascular cognitive impairment; management is control of the vascular risk factors, secondary prevention matched to the mechanism, review of the anticholinergic burden, and treatment of coexisting Alzheimer pathology where biomarkers support it.

medication_review.proposed: review of the current medication list for anticholinergic burden
warnings: Anticholinergic load is a reversible contributor to cognitive impairment in this population and should be quantified before any new prescription.
medication_review.summary: No prohibitive interaction identified within the current list.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Vascular dementia — multi-infarct type from symptomatic left internal carotid stenosis with coexisting paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented on pacemaker interrogation; diagnosed on CT because MRI is contraindicated

differential.key_features: Cannot be excluded, because CT cannot grade medial temporal atrophy and the patient cannot have an MRI; recall is cue-responsive and the profile is executive and language-led, which argues against it, and the diagnostic limitation should be stated rather than hidden

Cannot be excluded on CT, which cannot show microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis; this is the limitation that matters most, because it bears directly on the safety of the anticoagulation the atrial fibrillation indicates
Periventricular low attenuation is present but cannot be graded reliably on CT, and the two cortical infarcts with a stepwise history are the substrate
Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is documented, but both cortical infarcts are ipsilateral to a 60-70% stenosis, so a large-artery mechanism is at least as likely and both need treating

differential.diagnosis: Recurrent transient ischaemic attacks without infarction
differential.key_features: Two chronic cortical infarcts are visible on CT

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a collateral history from an informant who sees the patient daily: the shape of the decline (abrupt, stepwise or gradual), whether any step can be dated to a cerebrovascular event, and which instrumental activities have been lost
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Two dateable steps with stable plateaus between them, cue-responsive memory, executive and language complaints and loss of instrumental independence, in a patient for whom MRI is contraindicated

optimal_actions.action: Perform a validated bedside cognitive assessment and record the per-domain profile and whether delayed recall improves with cueing
optimal_actions.expected_finding: MoCA 19/30 with executive, attentional and mild language impairment, cue-responsive recall, and right-sided pyramidal signs on a stepwise history

optimal_actions.action: Order the reversible-cause screen and the vascular-risk assays that will be treated (CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, folate, RPR, HIV, HbA1c, lipid panel)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Reversible causes excluded; LDL 96 mg/dL above the secondary-prevention target

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to look for atrial fibrillation as the embolic source and for the left ventricular hypertrophy of chronic hypertension
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Paced rhythm with sinus activity on the atrial channel and no atrial fibrillation during the recording; surface interpretation limited, so the device's stored atrial data becomes the decisive test

optimal_actions.action: Image the extracranial carotid arteries to establish whether a large-artery source accounts for the cortical infarcts
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Left internal carotid stenosis of 60-70% ipsilateral to both cortical infarcts — a large-artery mechanism identified with a modality unaffected by the pacemaker

optimal_actions.action: Order prolonged ambulatory rhythm monitoring: a single ECG in sinus rhythm does not exclude paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, and finding it converts management from risk-factor control to anticoagulation
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Pacemaker interrogation shows a 2.1% atrial fibrillation burden with the longest episode over 6 hours — paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented from stored device data, adding a second mechanism

optimal_actions.action: Order formal multi-domain neuropsychological testing to settle the executive-versus-amnestic attribution and to document a baseline for follow-up
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Left-hemisphere-weighted profile with executive and naming involvement and preserved recognition, consistent with the CT-visible infarcts

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a head CT because MRI is contraindicated in this patient, and state the limitation: CT shows established infarcts and gross white matter change but cannot show microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis, so amyloid angiopathy cannot be excluded on it
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Two chronic left hemispheric cortical infarcts with periventricular low attenuation — sufficient for the vascular attribution, with the explicit limitation that CT cannot show microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis and therefore cannot exclude amyloid angiopathy

optimal_actions.action: Confirm the diagnostic criteria applied and the current secondary-prevention targets against the guidelines
optimal_actions.expected_finding: VASCOG 2014 criteria and the 2021 AHA/ASA secondary prevention targets confirmed

optimal_actions.action: Review the medication list for anticholinergic burden and for the interaction between antithrombotic choice and the microbleed burden before prescribing
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Anticholinergic contributors identified and the antithrombotic choice reconciled with the imaging burden

optimal_actions.action: Work within the imaging constraint and state it: attribute the dementia to the CT-visible infarcts while recording explicitly that amyloid angiopathy and coexisting Alzheimer pathology cannot be excluded; interrogate the pacemaker rather than fitting an external monitor; start anticoagulation for the documented atrial fibrillation after explaining that the haemorrhagic risk cannot be fully assessed without gradient-echo imaging, and stop the aspirin; refer for carotid revascularisation assessment for the symptomatic 60-70% stenosis; and intensify blood-pressure and lipid control
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Diagnosis established on CT with its limitations recorded, the pacemaker used as a continuous rhythm monitor, anticoagulation started with the unquantifiable haemorrhagic risk explained, and revascularisation assessment arranged

optimal_actions.action: Disclose the diagnosis and its mechanism to the patient and the informant, and address driving, medication management, finances, advance care planning and caregiver support
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Patient and informant engaged in care planning; safety domains addressed

useless_tools.rationale: EEG has no diagnostic role in vascular cognitive impairment; it belongs to the differential of a rapidly progressive or fluctuating course (Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, non-convulsive status, toxic-metabolic encephalopathy), none of which is present here

A presynaptic dopaminergic study answers the Lewy-body question, not the vascular one, and there is no spontaneous parkinsonism, no fluctuating cognition with hallucinations and no REM sleep behaviour disorder
Cardiac sympathetic imaging is a test for dementia with Lewy bodies and for autonomic failure; it says nothing about cerebrovascular disease

An untargeted paraneoplastic or autoimmune-encephalitis battery in a chronic stepwise decline with a hypertensive imaging burden is the archetypal expensive miss; the indication for those assays is a subacute multidomain syndrome

harmful_tools.rationale: The pacemaker and leads are not MR-conditional and the manufacturer's documentation is unavailable, so scanning risks lead heating, device damage and arrhythmia in a pacing-dependent patient with complete atrioventricular block; severe claustrophobia is an additional obstacle

sequence_constraints.reason: Document the cognitive deficit before attributing it: imaging read without a cognitive profile invites over-attribution of incidental white matter change

critical_actions: Confirm the MR-conditional status of the device and document why MRI cannot be performed rather than simply omitting it
Obtain CT and state explicitly what it cannot show — microbleeds, cortical superficial siderosis and medial temporal atrophy grade
Interrogate the pacemaker: it holds twelve months of continuous atrial rhythm data and outperforms any external monitor
Image the carotid arteries, since duplex ultrasound is unaffected by the device
Make the anticoagulation decision explicitly, acknowledging that the haemorrhagic risk cannot be fully assessed without gradient-echo imaging
Refer for revascularisation assessment of a symptomatic 60-70% stenosis and treat both mechanisms
contraindicated_actions: Do not scan a patient with a non-MR-conditional pacemaker and unavailable device documentation, particularly when pacing-dependent with complete atrioventricular block
Do not fit an external rhythm monitor when the implanted device already stores twelve months of atrial data
Do not present a CT-based diagnosis as equivalent to an MRI-based one — record the limitations, especially the inability to exclude amyloid angiopathy
Do not continue aspirin alongside a new anticoagulant without a separate indication
Do not withhold anticoagulation solely because microbleed status is unknown, but do document the uncertainty and the discussion
key_reasoning_points: A contraindication to the best test is a clinical problem to be worked around and documented, not a reason to leave the diagnosis unstated: CT plus the clinical course plus duplex plus device data reached a mechanism-level diagnosis here
The device in the patient is the best rhythm monitor available to him — twelve months of continuous stored atrial data at no additional cost and with no additional procedure

What CT cannot see is the clinically important part: microbleeds and siderosis bear directly on the safety of the anticoagulation the atrial fibrillation indicates, and that uncertainty must be named in the record and in the consent discussion
Two ipsilateral cortical infarcts downstream of a 60-70% stenosis and a documented 2.1% atrial fibrillation burden are two mechanisms, and each carries its own treatment
Stating a diagnostic limitation is part of the diagnosis; presenting a CT-based attribution as complete would misrepresent what is known

red_herrings.data_point: A pacemaker that appears to rule out further imaging
red_herrings.intended_effect: Leads to abandoning the mechanism workup and treating empirically, or to accepting an unexplained dementia
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: CT, carotid duplex and pacemaker interrogation together identified two treatable mechanisms; the device that blocked the MRI provided the rhythm data that no external monitor could match

red_herrings.intended_effect: Read as a Fazekas-equivalent burden sufficient to diagnose subcortical small-vessel vascular dementia
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: White matter change cannot be graded reliably on CT, and the two chronic cortical infarcts with a stepwise history are the demonstrated substrate

key_educational_points: A non-MR-conditional device is a documented contraindication, and the workup must be rebuilt around it rather than abandoned
An implanted pacemaker stores continuous atrial rhythm data that outperforms any external monitor
CT cannot show microbleeds or siderosis, so amyloid angiopathy cannot be excluded — a limitation that bears directly on anticoagulation
Naming the limitations of the available imaging is part of making the diagnosis

panel_required_exemptions.analyze_brain_mri: MRI is contraindicated in this patient: a non-MR-conditional pacemaker with unavailable device documentation in a pacing-dependent patient with complete atrioventricular block. The diagnosis is reached on CT, carotid duplex and pacemaker interrogation, and the ground truth requires stating what CT cannot exclude. `analyze_brain_mri` is classified harmful here, which is the whole point of the case.
